h: Caves, Puzzles and Steam in the Forest
p: The Forest of Dean is full of places with real character, and several of them are an easy drive from Beechenhurst. Puzzlewood near Coleford is an otherworldly tangle of mossy rocks, twisting paths and little bridges that's been used as a filming location for fantasy films and TV. Clearwell Caves takes you underground into old iron mines, which makes a cool, quiet contrast after all that time up high.

Steam fans can ride the Dean Forest Railway, a heritage line running through the southern part of the forest, and if you head west towards the Wye, Symonds Yat Rock gives you one of the most famous viewpoints in the area, looking down over a great loop in the river.

For the treetop course itself, a couple of hours is about right, and it's worth fitting your session in before the sculpture trail rather than after, while everyone's still fresh. Bring water for the climb and save the picnic for later; it'll taste twice as good once you've earned it.

Close to Beechenhurst, the Speech House, a historic hunting lodge turned hotel at the centre of the forest, is a handy landmark and a nice spot for a drink. All in all, this corner of the Dean can easily stretch to a long weekend, so don't try to cram it into one rushed afternoon.
